bull.b: The 20-year Rockdale lease adds a durable contracted-revenue base beyond volatile Bitcoin mining. Its 191 MW commitment, projected $9.1 billion initial-term revenue and 80%–90% illustrative NOI margin could materially improve recurring cash earnings once phased capacity is delivered.

AMD capacity has expanded to 50 MW, with the first 25 MW delivered on time and on budget and full deployment expected by May 2027. This provides an operating track record, recurring infrastructure revenue, and a foundation for further customer expansion.

Engineering revenue more than tripled year over year, gross margin expanded above 27%, and backlog reached $177.1 million, about 90% data center. The segment's manufacturing expansion and vertical capabilities can support timely deployments while diversifying revenue beyond mining.

bear.b: TTM profitability is severely impaired: gross margin is below zero, net margin is about -196%, and ROE is roughly -48%. The return from 2024 profitability to deep 2025 and TTM losses signals an unstable cost structure and weak current capital efficiency.

Using mined Bitcoin to fund data-center equity needs reduces the treasury asset available for future flexibility and ties development funding to asset sales. This increases reliance on external financing or continued monetization of Bitcoin while construction remains capital intensive.

Bitcoin mining remains exposed to lower Bitcoin prices and rising global hash-rate competition, which can compress revenue and mining economics independently of Riot's execution. That sensitivity may continue to create earnings volatility while the company transitions toward data-center revenue.
